title: Event-driven KPI aggregator for per-request attribution and tail-latency bucketing
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: We currently emit raw request counters and basic latency histograms but lack a scalable, low-cost mechanism to attribute tail latency and error spikes to request features (model, route, sequence_length_bucket, quantization profile). This causes slow incident debugging and prevents automated rollback/traffic shaping based on fine-grained KPIs.

Goal: Implement an event-driven KPI aggregator that consumes OTLP/Prometheus-derived events (request-level summaries and sampling traces), enriches them with routing and model metadata, computes lightweight per-request attribution (including tail-latency bucketing and error tags), and exports derived metrics to Prometheus and a secondary time-series datastore for SLO and dashboarding. The aggregator should be horizontally scalable, cost-efficient, and compatible with existing sampling and tracing hooks.
acceptance_criteria:
- Aggregator consumes OTLP/HTTP ingest events and sampled trace IDs.
- Produces derived Prometheus metrics: inference_request_tail_latency_bucket{model,route,seq_len_bucket,quant_profile}, inference_error_rate_by_variant{model,variant,region}.
- Adds labels for canary/dedicated/private routes and quantization profile.
- P99 tail attribution pipeline end-to-end latency <= 10s for steady state.
- Backfill/consistency validation against baseline Prometheus histograms (delta < 5% for core routes).
- Unit and integration tests covering enrichment, deduplication, and label cardinality controls.
- Dashboard panels added to latency/error dashboards and smoke queries validated by SRE and PM.
- Migration plan documented and no customer-facing downtime during rollout.
technical_design:
- Input: OTLP span attributes + compact per-request summary events emitted by the gateway sidecar.
- Processing: Use an event-driven service (kafka/ksql or Pulsar) to fan-in events; a stateless enrichment worker attaches model/route metadata via a fast in-memory cache and applies cardinality controls (label whitelists + hashing for long-tail values).
- Aggregation: Compute per-request buckets (latency buckets optimized for generation latency distribution) and emit derived metrics as counter increments using Prometheus remote-write and an async connector to our TSDB for long-term retention.
- Tracing hooks: correlate sampled spans by request_id to attach detailed debug attributes when present.
- Resilience: implement idempotency keys and short dedupe window (30s) to prevent double-counting on retries.
- Cost controls: enforce max label cardinality per metric and fallback to hashed label for uncommon values.
- Observability: internal metrics for input lag, processing rate, dropped events, and cardinality truncations.
- Tech stack considerations: prototype on kstream + go worker; evaluate moving critical hot-path to Rust for lower p99.
- Security: respects PII redaction rules and KMS-encrypted service credentials.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged canary in test region with 1% of traffic; 2) Validate derived metrics vs baseline histograms for core routes for 24h; 3) Gradually increase to 25%/50%/100% with rollback gates on divergence and error increase; 4) Flip to primary exporter and disable backfilling after stable run; 5) Deprecate noisy legacy metrics with a 2-week notice to consumers.
migration_steps:
- Deploy enrichment workers behind feature flag.
- Start emitting derived metrics in parallel (safe double-write).
- Run nightly reconciliation job to compare derived metrics to existing histograms and surface anomalies.
- Coordinate with dashboard owners to switch panels to new metrics.
- Remove legacy emitters after two stable weeks and notify downstream consumers.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for enrichment rules, label whitelisting, and dedupe logic.
- Integration tests using a synthetic traffic generator to validate p99 attribution and bucket correctness.
- Load test to validate end-to-end latency at target throughput (peak 10k req/s).
- Chaos test: worker restart, partition rebalances, and delayed OTLP events.
- Runbook validation with SRE on incident simulation (high-error spike ingestion).
monitoring_and_alerting:
- Alerts: high dropped_events_rate > 0.5% for 10m, input_lag > 30s, derived_export_errors > 1m.
- Dashboards: processing throughput, per-metric cardinality, label truncation rate, reconciliation delta vs baseline.
- On-call runbook: immediate rollback to double-write mode and scale up enrichment workers.
risk_and_mitigation:
- Cardinality explosion: mitigation via label whitelisting, hashed fallback, and metric sampling.
- Double counting on retries: dedupe keys and idempotency windows.
- Regressions in SLOs: gradual rollout with reconciliation checks and automatic rollback.
- PII leakage: strictly enforce redaction rules at gateway emitters and in enrichment workers.
